newsitem.title: FINLAND: Lively Helsinki surges on Nokia's third-quarter result.
newsitem.headline: Lively Helsinki surges on Nokia's third-quarter result.

text.p: A rally in telecommunications group Nokia following its third-quarter earnings report buoyed the HEX index to a new 2,349.57 point record, but the stock market closed slighly off that peak.
The HEX closed at 2,338.39, up 3.32 percent. Volume was massive for the Helsinki bourse, reaching 1.2 billion markka, with almost 80 percent of total turnover in Nokia.
Nokia closed heavy trade at 249.50 markka, up 22.50 markka or about 10 percent, its highest since October 23, 1995, after peaking at 254.00 markka during the session.
"No wonder Nokia rose like that. It was a very good result," one broker said of Nokia's January-September pre-tax profit of 2.23 billion markka, which matched analysts' forecasts.
Analysts particularly cheered the return to rapid growth of Nokia's mobile phones division, which they said could signal the end of its logistics problems.
Nokia held gains as New York opened, and hit $55-1/2 or about 252 markka in early trade, but Helsinki's strong tone was slightly muffled by early losses in U.S. paper stocks, brokers said.

Nevertheless, Finnish cyclical stocks tracked Nokia higher in moderate trade and Finland's biggest forestry group UPM-Kymmene, which holds about nine percent of votes in Nokia, closed lively trade up 2.10 markka at 91.10.
UPM sent other forestries advancing around two percent and the forestry sub-index ended 2.21 percent higher at 2044.16.
A Reuter poll of 14 Finnish analysts before Nokia's result showed that the HEX was expected to stand around 2,280 points at the end of 1996.
The average of the forecasts would mean a 33 percent rise for the HEX index compared to end-1995.
